Thought: Interim report with all human results pending; pipeline/provenance contribution is solid, honest about limits (gatekeeper sensitivity 2/6, pilot audits 6% > 2%). Core claim (accuracy) unsupported by design. Dense, many numbers; no baseline; same-family judge.
Summary: GP-RareLink presents a provenance-first pipeline (SLIDERS-style, run with Claude Opus) turning case reports into GA4GH Phenopackets with verbatim quotes and three-state HPO, a Claude gatekeeper pass, and a held-out evaluation against ClinVar/OMIM (concordance, gap candidates, bias, efficiency). Across six registered diseases (350 papers, 2,836 phenopackets) it reports complete quote coverage (by construction), low gatekeeper-flagged unsupported rates (0.43%), low HGVS recall vs ClinVar (10-35%), 57% OMIM recovery, and 214 untriaged gap candidates. All human-rated accuracy outcomes are pending; the only human audits (pilot, single rater, pre-freeze) exceeded the 2% target.
Strengths: Exceptionally candid framing: distinguishes provenance/feasibility from accuracy, reports unfavorable pilot audits and gatekeeper low sensitivity.
Pre-registration, frozen pipeline, ground-truth isolation test, seeded audit drawn before concordance; power/operating characteristics of rule C stated.
Large, concrete scale and clear three-state, quoted record design with deterministic span check.
Thoughtful held-out design (ClinVar/OMIM as scorers only), OMIM holdout with access analysis showing recovery bounded by literature access.
Careful interval reporting (exact/Wilson) and extensive limitations.
Weaknesses: The central claim (accuracy, <2% unsupported) is untested: primary O1, triage, adjudication, bias and efficiency are all pending, and the only human evidence (6.0%, 6.3%, one rater, earlier versions) is above target; the contribution is thus largely engineering/provenance, with 100% quote coverage true by construction and uninformative.

Validity of automated evaluation is weak: gatekeeper is same-family Claude with measured sensitivity of 2/6 and 1/4 (tiny n), so 0.43% is uninterpretable; HGVS recall of 10-35% is untriaged and confounded by ClinVar citation practice, conversion errors and access; overlap is not precision; no baseline (e.g., simple tagger, single-pass LLM, other model) or ablation shows the pipeline components matter.

Methodological concerns: HA20 development-disease tuning and ClinVar-seeded corpus; frozen known gap (no hedge rule) deliberately left; only 28% open full text so selected, non-random literature; deduplication weak (6/93 false merges in pilot, 50-merge hand check not done); calibration set rule amended after labels and single-person reference; open-weight comparison unaudited and judged by Claude.

Presentation: extremely dense, number-heavy text with many post-hoc deviations, extension/exploratory/addendum strands and pending boxes that hinder reading; ICLR template for an interim internal report; novelty relative to LitVar/AVADA/phenopacket-store-style extraction is argued but not demonstrated empirically.
Questions: What is the O1 result and does rule C pass; what does the gatekeeper catch on those 250 claims?
How does a simple baseline (single-pass Claude without gatekeeper, or an existing tool) compare on the same audit?
What fraction of low HGVS recall remains after triage?
How were the 6 false merges addressed and what is the final merge error rate?
How sensitive are results to the HA20 tuning and to hedge-rule omission?
Limitations: Authors thoroughly list limitations (single rater pilot, same-family judge, open-access selection, dedup, no re-audit of frozen pipeline); additionally, no baseline comparison and same model family drafted the report.
